# Building

```sh
./setup.sh --sly2 /path/to/SCUS_973.16
make elf
```

`setup.sh` checks the executable's SHA-1, copies it to `work/elf/`, creates `.venv` from `requirements.txt` and
downloads the R5900 binutils into `tools/` (pinned SHA-256; Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64 builds; use WSL or Docker
elsewhere). Nothing proprietary is stored in the repository.

`make elf` runs `configure.py --split`, ninja, `scripts/build/link_image.py` and `scripts/verify_image.py`:

1. Splat (`config/us/sly2.us.yaml`, generated by `make config` from `config/recovered/modules.tsv`) splits the executable into one assembly file per module (430 units in `build/splat/asm/<module>.s`, named like the folders of `src/`) and raw pieces
   (`assets/*.databin.bin`): the VU1 microcode, the embedded IOP modules, and the ELF header and tail. The rodata and
   data are cut into 335 per-module pieces (`config/us/pieces.tsv`: each address the code names is given to the first
   unit, in code order, that refers to it) and disassembled per symbol (`asm/data/{rodata,data}/<module>.*.s`: a label
   at every referenced address, pointers as symbol names). Names come from
   `config/recovered/sly2_combined_symbol_addrs.txt` (generated by `scripts/names/combine.py` from the evidenced and the provisional names) through `scripts/names/export_splat_symbols.py`.
2. ninja wraps the raw pieces as objects (`include/macro.inc` holds the label macros) and compiles every matched
   function of `src/` with the original compiler (SN ProDG EE-GCC 2.95.3 build 1.36, `-O2 -G0 -ffast-math
   -fno-exceptions`, run through wibo) and the original assembler ([ps2eeas](assembler.md)), keeping only the code of each object.
3. `link_image.py` drops the assembly of every function that has a compiled object, assembles the rest in runs, links
   everything at the retail addresses (`config/us/image.ld`) and compares each swapped function with the retail
   bytes, and assembles the per-symbol data pieces and compares them too. A function whose object does not reproduce them (it names a symbol the table does
   not know, say) falls back to assembly; an object with helpers before or after the function is cut to the function, and one
   whose string literals sit in another order in the retail rodata is linked with the retail addresses (each string is
   checked); the link is repeated until none differ. The result is `build/image/image.bin`;
   `build/image/fallbacks.tsv` says why functions fell back. A data piece that does not reproduce its bytes, or that
   holds the rodata of a function linked from C (the object's section takes that range), is linked from the raw
   retail bytes instead.
4. `pack_elf.py` assembles the whole file (`build/image/SCUS_973.16`) from the image and the container pieces, and
   `scripts/verify_image.py` compares every loaded byte and then the whole file with the retail executable. A good run
   ends with the SHA-1 of the retail file and `PASS: reconstructed image matches retail`.

| Command | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `make elf` | split, compile, link and verify the executable image (the gate) |
| `make objdiff` | after `make elf`: `objdiff.json`, the objects it compares (retail assembly per unit against the unit's compiled functions) and `site/data/objdiff-report.json` |
| `make config` | regenerate `config/us/sly2.us.yaml` (the per-module split) |
| `make src` | publish the matched functions from `data/matching/src` into `src/` |
| `make progress` | after `make elf`: `site/data/report.json`, `site/progress-map.svg` and the site assets (the progress page in `site/`, deployed by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`) |
| `make check` | script syntax, shellcheck, markdown links |

## Checks

| Where | What |
| :--- | :--- |
| `make help` | Lists the targets |
| `make check` | Runs ruff (`pyproject.toml`: syntax errors and undefined names), byte-compiles the scripts, shellchecks, checks the links of the markdown files and runs `scripts/test_public_tools.py` |
| `make unit UNIT=<module>` | After `make elf`: do the matched functions of a module (or an address, or a `src/` file) link from C? Says why not when they fall back |
| `python3 scripts/list_functions.py` | Lists functions from `site/data/report.json` (filter by module, status, size) to choose the next one |
| `checks` workflow | The `make check` steps, plus the commit messages and the pull request title |
| `cleanup` workflow | [docs/contributing/code-cleanup.md](../contributing/code-cleanup.md) on the code a pull request adds |
| `progress` + `progress-comment` workflows | Validate the committed `site/data/summary.json` and comment the change against `main` on a pull request |
| `pages` workflow | Deploys `site/` |
| dependabot | Keeps the pinned actions and the pinned `requirements.txt` current (monthly) |

None of the workflows builds the game: that needs your own executable and the compiler, so `make elf` stays a local gate.
Its expected SHA-1 is `config/us/checksum.sha1`, read by `setup.sh` and `scripts/verify_image.py`.

## Status

The gate passes: the image is rebuilt with 3,437 functions from the compiled C of `src/` and 3,365 from generated
assembly (1.95 MB of code, VU microcode, rodata and data, plus 474 KB of IOP modules). 3,448 functions are matched by
the judge. Of those, 8 still come from assembly (`build/image/fallbacks.tsv`, and a few too large for their slot):

- names the symbol table lacks (C++ constructors, library calls) are read from the retail instruction at each
  relocation site, so those functions link without a table entry;
- a function's own jump table or literals (`.rodata` of its object, cut at its content: the section is padded to its alignment, a 14-entry table becoming 64 bytes, and the padding would overwrite the retail bytes after it) are linked where the retail image has them: the
  retail rodata is split around that range and the object's section takes its place.

The ELF container is carried as raw pieces cut from your executable: the header and program headers, the padding, the
section data outside the loaded segments (overlay tables, `.mdebug`) and the section header table. The code, the VU1
microcode, the rodata, the data and the IOP modules are the rebuilt image, and the whole file matches the retail SHA-1.
Rodata and data are per-symbol assembly (306 of the 335 pieces; the rest stay raw bytes, see above); function-owned
rodata comes from the compiled objects.

objdiff (`make objdiff`) pairs each function of a unit's retail assembly with the compiled one by name and counts
matched code per unit; the "Data" category adds a unit per retail data section (`data/rodata`, `data/data`, `data/vutext`, `data/irx`, from `work/elf/SCUS_973.16`; sizes only, no bytes reach the report) with an empty compiled side, and `data/rodata-c`: the rodata that compiled C objects own (their own jump tables and literals, the `.ro_<address>` sections of the linked image), which is the only data counted as matched (84 ranges, 3,700 of 1,011,732 bytes). objdiff counts a data section as matched only when all of it matches, so the C-owned ranges are a unit of their own; its numbers are in `site/data/objdiff-report.json` and on the progress page. Windows: use WSL.
The compiler is run on Linux with wibo (32-bit), on macOS with wibo-macos.


## Other versions (PAL)

`python3 scripts/disc_extract.py discs/<disc>.iso` reads a disc image (ISO 9660, 2048-byte sectors) and writes the boot executable named by `SYSTEM.CNF` to `work/elf/`; `--list` shows the root directory. The PAL disc (Europe, v2.01, `SCES_525.29`, VMODE=PAL) has the same section layout as the US executable: `.text` is 0x15A840 bytes against 0x159DF0 (+0.2%), `.vutext` and `.irx` are the same size, `.rodata` grows by 26 KB, `.data` by 0x1C0.

`.venv/bin/python scripts/pair_versions.py` pairs the US functions with the other version's and writes `config/eu/map.tsv` (`us_address`, `other_address`, `size`, `status`; addresses only). Both `.text` sections are read as words with the targets of `j`/`jal` and the immediates of the address-forming instructions dropped, so a function that moved but did not change reads the same in both. A US function is `identical` (raw bytes equal), `same` (the same instructions: only an address or a constant differs), `gap` (paired by position inside two gaps of equal length) or `none`. For the PAL v2.01 executable: 1,002 identical, 4,860 same (89.2% of the code), 823 gap, 67 none. `same` does not yet say that the C of a matched US function reproduces the PAL bytes: that needs the addresses it refers to resolved in PAL, which the next step derives from the paired functions' `lui`/`addiu` pairs.
